question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{4x+1} & ={6}^{7x+5} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{4x+1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{7x+5})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(4x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)=(7x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(4x+1)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(7x+5)\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)+5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ 4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x & =\frac{5\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}{4\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-7\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
